root_idea.summary: The supplied lexical evidence centers on the hard outer shell of an egg, a covering that takes hold of what it encloses; in the Quranic Form II construction, this image motivates assigning an associate that takes hold of a person.
root_idea.development: The shell image is extended to appointing, preparing, or bringing one person or thing into relation with another. The wider lexical record also preserves separate branches involving cleaving, equivalence, substitution, and exchange.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Quran-attested Form II verb with direct lexical evidence; displayed under its normalized perfect-tense dictionary citation form.

senses.definition: To ordain, appoint, prepare, or bring a person or thing for someone; in the Quranic construction, to assign an associate or companion that takes hold of the person.
senses.usage_conditions: Used with لِـ for the person for whom someone or something is appointed. The Quranic usage includes associates and a devil appointed so as to gain possession or control, expressed through the image of an egg-shell taking hold of the egg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cleave, break, or rend asunder; to crack a glass vessel without separating its parts; and, in a dialectal usage, to demolish or throw down a building.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively and intransitively. It may describe an egg becoming cleft, a tooth falling from its root, or similar breaking and separation phenomena.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To hollow out or dig a well in rock; to be dug.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the excavation of a well or similar hollowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To liken or assimilate one person or thing to another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with بِـ to express the person or thing to which another is likened.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To barter or exchange one commodity or thing for another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exchange is reciprocal in effect: one party gives an item and takes another in its place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To break into pieces; of a wall, to fall into ruins or break down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of eggs, glass vessels, walls, and similar objects. This is distinct in form from the Quranic Form II verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become ordained, appointed, or prepared for someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive or reflexive construction describing something becoming assigned or made available for a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To resemble another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source attests the construction with a person as object, including the expression ‘to resemble his father’; the meaning is not restricted to fathers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To barter or exchange commodities mutually.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of two parties exchanging with each other; it is the reciprocal counterpart of barter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To crack or split, especially without complete separation; by extension, to fall into pieces, collapse, or split lengthwise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Of an egg or glass bottle, it may crack without splitting apart. Of a wall, tooth, or well, the sources report variants including cracking, falling, splitting lengthwise, or collapsing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To extirpate or destroy utterly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive Form VIII usage describing complete destruction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To receive or take something in exchange.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form VIII exchange usage, comparable to taking something by way of compensation or substitution.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hard upper shell or covering of an egg; also the shell when cracked into pieces or left after the young bird or fluid has gone out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers specifically to the outer covering of an egg and its broken or emptied state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A compensation, substitute, equivalent, or thing given, received, or put in place of another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The same noun may describe two persons or things that are alike or mutually suitable as substitutes, and something equivalent to another.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A small piece of bone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal usage with the plural form reported separately in the lexical evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A barterer or exchanger of commodities.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal noun for one who exchanges goods.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place containing an egg-shell or the outer part of an egg called قَيْض.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place noun associated with the shell or outer covering of an egg.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An egg that has been cleft or split.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive construction applied to an egg that has opened or split.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A well abounding in water, understood as having been hollowed out or cleft.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive construction applied to a well in relation to its excavation or hollowed condition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who gives or receives something in exchange.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the party involved in bartering, especially the receiver of an exchanged item.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cracked without being split apart, especially an egg or glass vessel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive form for an egg or glass bottle with a crack that does not divide it completely; variant analyses of related forms are reported in the lexical tradition.
